name: Bridge Across the Gaussian Moat

phase_0.boundary_condition: The infinite lattice of Gaussian integers Z[i]

VINIT.justification: The uninitialized starting point in the complex plane before any path construction begins.

TANCH.justification: The terminal boundary that the path seeks to reach or prove unreachable.

AFWD.justification: A forward movement to a neighboring Gaussian integer within the step size limit k.

AREV.justification: Reversing a step to explore an alternative branch of the search tree.

CLINK.justification: The composition of individual steps into a continuous walk across the lattice.

IMSCRIB.justification: The identity check that confirms a coordinate is a Gaussian prime.

FSPLIT.justification: The branching of potential next steps into prime and non-prime (moat) candidates.

FFUSE.justification: The reunification of branch evaluations into a single confirmed position on the lattice.

EVALT.justification: Successful identification of a Gaussian prime within reach.

EVALF.justification: Identification of a region of composite numbers exceeding the step bound.

ENGAGR.justification: A state where a path is neither blocked nor infinite, held in the tension of the conjecture.

IFIX.justification: The permanent fixation of a verified path segment or a proven moat boundary.

phase_3.void_description: The empty set of coordinates before path initialization.
phase_3.true_description: A valid step onto a Gaussian prime.
phase_3.false_description: An invalid step into a composite moat.
phase_3.both_description: The undecidable state of a path that has not yet reached a moat or infinity.

steps.domain_action: Initialize search at the origin of the complex plane
Identify the origin as a starting Gaussian prime
Record the origin as the first node in the path
Branch search into all possible steps of size k
Move toward a candidate coordinate in the T-branch
Verify if the candidate is a Gaussian prime
Confirm the coordinate is a prime and valid for landing
Move toward a candidate coordinate in the F-branch
Verify if the candidate is a composite number
Confirm the coordinate is part of a potential moat
Reconstitute the local topology around the current node
Chain the successful T-branch step to the existing path
Append the new prime coordinate to the permanent path record
Branch again to check for path termination or continuation
Hold the state of a path that is currently bounded but not yet blocked
Resolve the path state into the next iteration of the search
Define the global boundary of the Gaussian integer lattice

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The primality testing algorithm for Gaussian integers
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The adjacency relation between lattice points in Z[i]
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The stack of visited coordinates and the current path length
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The breadth-first or depth-first search priority for path expansion
phase_5.alfs_store: The fundamental theorem of arithmetic in the Gaussian integers

phase_6.cycle_cost: Computational cycles required for primality testing and step validation
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A known path of length N
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A known path of length N+1 or a proven boundary
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The information gained about the lattice structure is conserved within the proof state.
